name: The Babeu household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: babeu_joseph

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 January 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-03-04, 62 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-01-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1834-01-01 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THE SEASON AND NOTHING ELSE. No trade is recorded for this household and no source says why it came; the only thing the evidence gives is when it was here by. This states the draws that were operating in that season and chooses among them nowhere. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

persons.note: KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Joseph Babeu' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 4 March 1834, column 33 — dated 1834-03-04. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

merge_ruling.for_merge: One letter at the end of a French-Canadian surname, an identical forename, one office, one paper and one kind of list. Babeu and Babeue are the same word with and without its terminal e, the Chicago post office held a letter for each inside six months, and the town's whole knowledge of both is those two lines. On resemblance alone this is the most merge-like pair of the seven.
merge_ruling.against_merge: TWO RETURNS, AND NEITHER SETS BOTH. “Joseph Babeu” is LINE 10 of the return of 1 January 1834, read at the page image by T-0424 and tied there by T-1010's concordance to the one impression that carries it, the Democrat of 4 March 1834, column 33 — a single tie, no second reading, no disagreement on the row. “Joseph Babeue” stands on the return of 1 July 1834, printed in the impressions of 9 July (“oseph Babeue”, the initial lost) and 16 July 1834 (“Joseph Babeue”) — two impressions of that later return, agreeing with each other and both against the January spelling. So the office closed two returns six months apart, entered one spelling on each, and was never asked to set them together: C9's demonstration is absent and D5's is absent with it. Neither card is an anchor — no trade, no dwelling, no research on either — and neither name appears anywhere else in the corpus; the gazetteer holds these two and no other bearer of the stem. What is left to fold on is one letter, which is what T-1001 measured and refused. D6, and the cards stay two.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
